item.title: [LINGUIST List — Calls for Papers] Calls: Journal of Estonian and Finno-Ugric Linguistics - "Special Issue - From Home Language to Language of Schooling: Multilingual Students, Teachers, and Educational Change in Estonia and Beyond" (Jrnl)
item.description: Estonia continues to address the social, political, and demographic legacies of its Soviet past, most notably the dual school system, which has contributed to broader social segregation. At the same time, this system also reflects a longer historical tradition, predating the Soviet era, of educating students separately according to their native languages. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: Formal Diachronic Semantics 10
item.description: The meeting Formal Diachronic Semantics brings together research on meaning change in natural language and its origins in, and effects on pragmatics and semantics, and their interfaces with morphosyntax and prosody. Special attention is given to studies that are related to formal accounts of semantics and grammar, providing new insights into language specific as well as universal patterns in language. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Conference Announcements] Confs: Panel at NeMLA 2027: Linguistics, Language Attitudes, and Popular Culture (Panel)
item.description: The relationship of Linguistics, Language Attitudes, and Popular Culture is of paramount importance in understanding how meaning is constructed and communicated in our everyday lives. Exploring how language is used and the ideas, attitudes, and information it conveys, overtly and in more implicit ways in our popular culture allows us to better understand ourselves and the cultures we live in. item.description: The 4th edition of LingCor: Workshop on Spoken Corpus Linguistics will take place at the Institut für Romanistik of the Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin from the 5th till the 7th October 2026. item.title: [LINGUIST List — Calls for Papers] Calls: Languages - "Special Issue: Shifting Politeness in Multilingual Contexts: Address Forms in Migrant, Colonial, and Indigenous Languages" (Jrnl)
item.description: Forms of address are among the most sensitive linguistic indicators of social relations, politeness norms, and identity.
